key_insight: AI turbulence modeling should balance physical causation and statistical correlation according to flow memory and user intent, rather than use one approach for all flows.
engineering_relevance: The framework guides engineers toward local RANS closures near equilibrium, causal scale resolution for unseen non-equilibrium flows, or fast surrogate synthesis within known flow classes.
method: Use Mori–Zwanzig projection to separate turbulent stress into local response and non-local memory.
For unseen non-equilibrium flows, use Rules-Augmented AI to guide first-principles scale resolution.
For known parameterized flow classes, combine non-intrusive reduced-order modeling with uncentered POD across multi-realization ensembles.
evidence_signal: The abstract presents a theoretical framework but reports no quantitative benchmarks, dataset sizes, or validation metrics.
watch_item: Local closures remain engineering approximations even near equilibrium because pressure couples stress evolution to spatial structure beyond local velocity gradients.
paper_title: AI Meets Turbulence Modeling: Balancing Causation, Correlation, and User Intent
